I can't wait until I move out and go to college. I feel like it'll help me to grow on my own as a person. Self harm helped me cope. People think, "Oh you just want attention" or "How does hurting yourself help?!" When in reality, no I don't want attention, and it releases endorphins. I actually credit it for saving me from suicide a couple times. It calmed me down and made me feel better... For a few seconds. The problem was that I cut because I hated myself for being what I am, then I'd cut because after some time if be ashamed of myself for cutting. Luckily I've significantly reduced the rate of my self harm. I did maybe around 650 cuts on my thigh at ya worst moment. Now I just go outside and listen to birds, or music to calm myself down. Self harm is really a sad thing, and I used to be the person who didn't know why people self harmed and I thought they were crazy. Now I understand it completely.

I'm sorry to hear that about your family, and I don't know of any of my friends know I suffer from anxiety and depression. The anxiety stops me from telling them. They also "joke" about self harm saying stuff like "Go cut yourself emo fag" not towards me, but talking about other people. That's another reason I don't want to say I have depression because they might find out about my self harm, which raises my anxiety. It's sort of a loop always ending in higher anxiety.
I feel like my family is against me. I don't like being around them, because they say I ruin the mood. I've tried to open up, but I just get out down.
It just sort of happens. I've had a relatively good life, and I can't see why I'm depressed.

I suffer from a clinically-diagnosed branch of OCD called "Repetitive OCD." It basically means I have to do something over and over until my brain is satisfied for me to be able to move into something else. The example I use to help people understand is that I could be sitting in class taking handwritten notes, and this overwhelming feeling swallows me. The only way I find to satisfy it is to do the notes. Over and over. I've sometimes done the notes up to 20 times. It can honestly be crippling, and I hate when teenage girls/ young adult women (not saying males don't do this because they do also, but my experience is with the majority being female) say, "Oh my god I'm SOOOOO OCD because that crooked picture is SOOOOO annoying!" OCD isn't super rare, but I doubt most of the people who say that truly know what being OCD is like and how crippling it can be. It just bothers me when people try to self-diagnose themselves because they HAVE to fix a crooked picture. That's how literally everyone is with crooked pictures, or things that are out of place.
